title: Miko Kobi and DK Weekly Sync - 2026/06/08 13:01 EDT - Notes by Gemini
screen_reason: Jumpr-internal weekly sync, held one week before WagerTech kickoff. Short WagerTech passages give the client go-ahead and verbal commit, kickoff timing, rebuild scope, PRD status, Sales Cloud custom-object scope, the WhatsApp AI-extraction component, the payout logic, the seven-phase structure and post-build support. The rest of the meeting is other clients and Jumpr-internal matters and is not recorded.

items.statement: Miko told the team that Jumpr has the go-ahead from WagerTech. Later in the meeting he said WagerTech had given a verbal commitment, that the contract is 'as good as' signed, and that Jumpr has to deliver.
items.quote: Miko Sumagang: ... Um we've gotten a go ahead for wager tech. Okay. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Nice. / Miko Sumagang: ... the wager tech like people is basically as good as sign we got like verbal commit like already so like we have to like execute like for them
items.asr_note: 'as good as sign' = 'as good as signed' [ASR?]. Second quote is from line 645 (timestamp 00:46:34).
items.note: Jumpr-internal meeting; the client was not present. This is the Jumpr lead's internal account of the scope, not client-voiced evidence.

items.statement: WagerTech wants to kick off the week after this meeting (the week after 2026-06-08). Miko confirmed this.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: and widget techch wants to kick off next week. Eh, / Miko Sumagang: Yes. Yes.
items.asr_note: widget techch = WagerTech [ASR?]. Also stated at line 158: 'It's going to kick off next week.'
items.note: Jumpr-internal meeting; the client was not present. This is the Jumpr lead's internal account of the scope, not client-voiced evidence.

items.statement: The scope is a full rebuild: WagerTech's existing Salesforce org was built quickly with AI ('vibe coded') and Jumpr will remove what is there and build a new org.
items.quote: Miko Sumagang: It is uh a fairly simple like projects like the PD is like already like defined. We're basically just like creating um their sales course like org. It was vibe coded. We're ripping everything out and then we're putting in like the real meat like in it. / Miko Sumagang: ... So, we're ripping the whole s*** out and then we're building out like a a brand new like or for them.
items.asr_note: PD = PRD; sales course = Salesforce; 'or' = org [ASR?]
items.note: Jumpr-internal meeting; the client was not present. This is the Jumpr lead's internal account of the scope, not client-voiced evidence.

items.statement: The PRD is already written. Per Miko, the objects, fields and reports are already known, and Jumpr has a walkthrough of how WagerTech uses its current system.
items.quote: Miko Sumagang: ... what's cool about wager attack is the prd are all already designed we already know the objects. We already all know all the fields. We already know all the the reports. We have a walkthrough of like how they're using like the system.
items.note: Jumpr-internal meeting; the client was not present. This is the Jumpr lead's internal account of the scope, not client-voiced evidence.

items.feature_area: Other (AI extraction of WhatsApp messages into Salesforce records)
items.topic: AI WhatsApp message extraction to records
items.statement: WagerTech currently takes customers in through WhatsApp chats. Miko described an AI component that extracts the WhatsApp messages and creates records in Salesforce, with reporting after that. The approach is still being worked out (see the open question on the entry point). The timing is also unclear: at line 307 Miko says WagerTech wants 'AI' after the seven phases are done.
items.quote: Miko Sumagang: And the only complexity that's like left that we have to like figure out, which is actually like a very cool project to like work on is that they currently bring in customers via WhatsApp chats. / Miko Sumagang: ... and then we're creating uh an AI that would extract their WhatsApp messages so that it creates like records inside of Salesforce. That is like really what that is and then like reporting afterwards.
items.note: Jumpr-internal meeting; the client was not present. This is the Jumpr lead's internal account of the scope, not client-voiced evidence.

items.feature_area: Other (AI extraction of WhatsApp messages into Salesforce records)
items.statement: WagerTech cannot keep running on WhatsApp because of the high volume. Jumpr is still working out the most efficient entry point for the AI component.
items.quote: Miko Sumagang: Because there is this like AI component that goes like into this because like we cannot like have them like live off of like WhatsApp because like it's a high volume like setup ... / Miko Sumagang: ... So there is this like whole like AI component that we're like looking at to figure out like what would be like the / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. / Miko Sumagang: most like efficient like entry point like into this.
items.note: Jumpr-internal meeting; the client was not present. This is the Jumpr lead's internal account of the scope, not client-voiced evidence.

items.statement: Per Miko, the payout depends on three things together: the player who signed up, the player's location, and the sponsoring organization. Jumpr pays out that amount to people and tracks the payouts.
items.quote: Miko Sumagang: ... the permutation between the / Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. / Miko Sumagang: player who signed up and their location plus uh the organization that's like sponsoring it has a particular payout, / Kobi Kunasekaran: Oops. / Miko Sumagang: right? So you almost have to like do like that like permutation those like three uh considerations and then it comes off with like a payout and then that payout is like basically what we end up like paying out to like like the people and then we track like the payouts.
items.asr_note: 'we end up like paying out' is Miko's own analogy wording; in context the payer is WagerTech, not Jumpr.
items.note: Jumpr-internal meeting; the client was not present. This is the Jumpr lead's internal account of the scope, not client-voiced evidence.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: The team approved the Salesforce rebuild for Wager Tech.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Miko Sumagang: ... Um we've gotten a go ahead for wager tech. Okay.
gemini_disagreements.why: Wrong party. The transcript says Jumpr received the go-ahead from WagerTech (the client approved). The summary says 'the team approved'. At line 645 Miko also calls it a verbal commit, not a signed contract.

gemini_disagreements.summary_text: This engagement encompasses 7 phases and mandates AI integration for automated message extraction and record management.
gemini_disagreements.transcript_quote: Miko Sumagang: ... So there is this like whole like AI component that we're like looking at to figure out like what would be like the / Kobi Kunasekaran: Yeah. / Miko Sumagang: most like efficient like entry point like into this.
gemini_disagreements.why: Firmer than the transcript. Jumpr is still working out the approach and entry point for the AI component. At line 307 'AI' is something WagerTech wants after the seven phases. Nobody says AI is 'mandated'.

notes: Read all 963 lines. Pre-kickoff internal briefing. The client was not present, so every item is the Jumpr lead's internal account of the scope and should support client-meeting evidence, not replace it. Four WagerTech-adjacent passages were left out under rule 5 (pricing, staffing and internal tooling). They are not recorded here. Delivery ranges skip lines 300-304 (pricing). The business-model passage at lines 175-185 was used for context only. All other content (other clients, internal operations) was not extracted. No Jira keys were mentioned.
